text: how did the dinosaurs die out?
spoken: Mostly an asteroid. About sixty-six million years ago, a huge one hit what's now Mexico. It threw dust and debris into the air, blocking sunlight. Plants struggled, and food chains collapsed from the bottom up. Volcanic eruptions in India were also going on around then, so scientists think both played a part.

text: how did napoleon die?
spoken: Napoleon died in May 1821, in exile on the island of Saint Helena. The British had sent him there after Waterloo. The cause is debated. Doctors at the time pointed to stomach cancer, and many historians still agree. Arsenic poisoning is a popular theory, but I'm not sure it's been proven.

text: what killed the people at pompeii?
spoken: Mostly the volcano, but not the lava. Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 AD and threw ash and pumice into the sky for hours, and Pompeii was buried under it. Then came fast-moving clouds of superheated gas and ash, called pyroclastic surges. Those were the real killers.

text: why does romeo kill himself in the play?

text: why did socrates drink hemlock?
spoken: Because he was sentenced to death. In 399 BC an Athenian jury found him guilty of impiety and corrupting the young. Hemlock was the state's standard method of execution. He chose to accept the verdict rather than escape, even though friends offered him a way out.

text: how do antibiotics kill bacteria?
spoken: Short version, they attack things bacteria have and your cells don't. Many break the cell wall, so the bacterium bursts. Others jam its protein-making machinery, called ribosomes, so it can't grow or copy itself. That's why they work on bacteria but not viruses. Want me to go into one type, like penicillin?

text: why do leaves die in autumn?
spoken: Short days and cold tell the tree winter's coming. The tree stops making chlorophyll, the green pigment that traps sunlight. Then it seals off each leaf and pulls the useful nutrients back into the branches. That's why the yellows and oranges show up. They were hidden under the green all along.

text: how high can a cat fall and survive?
spoken: Honestly, it's surprisingly high. Vets studied cats that fell from tall buildings, and many survived falls of several storeys, but I'm not sure of an exact limit. Cats reach a top speed called terminal velocity, and after that they stop speeding up. They also relax and spread out like a parachute, which helps. Want to see how falling speed builds up?

text: what happens to a star when it dies?
spoken: That depends on how big the star is. A small star, like our sun, swells up into a red giant. Then it puffs off its outer layers and leaves a tiny, hot core called a white dwarf. A really massive star ends in a huge explosion, a supernova. What's left behind is either a neutron star or a black hole.

text: how long can a whale hold its breath?
spoken: Depends on the whale. Most big whales hold it for ten to thirty minutes. Sperm whales usually dive about forty-five minutes to an hour. The record belongs to Cuvier's beaked whale, over three hours in one study. It's not that their lungs are huge. They store oxygen in their blood and muscles instead.

text: how fast does a bullet train go?
spoken: Depends on the train. Most bullet trains run about two hundred to three hundred kilometres an hour. The fastest in regular service is Shanghai's maglev, around four hundred and thirty. I'm not sure of the exact figure for Japan's newest ones, so check that if you need it.

text: can you die from holding your breath?
spoken: Mostly no, not by holding it on purpose. Your body forces you to breathe once carbon dioxide builds up. If you pass out, breathing restarts on its own. The real danger is in water, where passing out can mean drowning. Is this for a biology question, or just curious?

text: how do you cut a cube to get a hexagon?
spoken: Nice puzzle, and it works. Picture a cube sitting on one corner. Slice with a flat plane straight through the middle, perpendicular to the line from that corner to the opposite corner. You cut through all six faces, so the edge of the cut has six sides.

text: whats the point of learning fractions?
spoken: Fair question. Fractions are how you talk about parts of things, and you use them constantly without noticing. Shooting percentage is one. Seven makes out of ten shots is seventy percent. Same idea shows up in recipes, discounts, and ratios. And algebra later leans on fractions everywhere, so it matters for your exam too.

text: which way do you cut a pizza for equal slices?
spoken: Good thing to ask, since cutting carefully is the whole trick. Actually, scratch the ball. Pizza's just a circle, so it's about angles. Every cut goes straight through the center. For eight slices, you want each angle the same. Three sixty divided by eight is forty-five degrees per slice.

text: what was the black death?
spoken: It was a plague pandemic that swept through Europe, Asia, and North Africa in the 1340s. It's usually blamed on a bacterium called Yersinia pestis, spread by fleas on rats. It killed a huge share of people, historians often say a third or more of Europe.

text: how did cleopatra die?
spoken: Traditionally, the story is that she died by snakebite, probably an asp, in 30 BCE, after Octavian's forces took Egypt. That's what ancient writers like Plutarch reported. Historians aren't sure it's true, though. Some think poison is likelier, and Octavian had reasons to want her gone.

text: why is cyanide poisonous?
spoken: Cyanide shuts down the part of your cells that uses oxygen. Inside your mitochondria, an enzyme called cytochrome c oxidase passes electrons to oxygen to make energy. Cyanide sticks to the iron in that enzyme and blocks it. So oxygen is in your blood but the cells can't use it.

text: how does anesthesia put you to sleep?
spoken: Short version, it turns down how your brain cells talk to each other. Most anesthetic drugs boost the brain's "slow down" signals, or block its "speed up" ones. With enough of that, the networks that make you aware and form memories can't work together. You're not just resting.

text: why did samurai practice seppuku?
spoken: Honor, mostly. Samurai saw it as a way to die on their own terms rather than be captured, shamed, or killed by an enemy. It also became a formal punishment. A lord could order a samurai to do it instead of facing a common execution, which let him keep his dignity.

text: how does a nuclear bomb work in simple terms?
spoken: Short version, it's a runaway chain reaction. Uranium or plutonium atoms split when a neutron hits them. Each split releases a huge burst of energy and more neutrons. Those neutrons split more atoms, and it doubles over and over. In a tiny fraction of a second, you get an enormous release of energy.

text: how do you stay safe in a thunderstorm?
spoken: Get indoors, into a proper building or a hard-topped car. Open spaces, tall trees, and water are the dangerous spots. Stay inside until thirty minutes after the last thunder you hear. If you can hear thunder, you're close enough to be struck. Want to know why the thunder and lightning come at different times?

text: what do lifeguards do when a swimmer is in danger?
spoken: Lifeguards watch constantly, scanning the water so they spot trouble early. A drowning swimmer often can't wave or shout. They look like they're quietly climbing an invisible ladder. The guard blows a whistle, grabs a flotation device, and reaches or throws it, or swims out with it.

text: why is it bad to mix bleach and ammonia?
spoken: Good thing to ask before it happens by accident. They react and make chloramine gases. Those burn your eyes, throat, and lungs, and can make breathing really hard. That's why cleaning products shouldn't be mixed, and bleach especially. Ammonia hides in glass cleaners and some others. If it happens, get out into fresh air and tell an adult. If someone's struggling to breathe, call your local emergency number.

text: is it dangerous to look at the sun?
spoken: Yes, it can be. Staring at the sun can burn the retina, the light-sensing layer at the back of your eye. The tricky part is that the retina has no pain sensors, so it doesn't hurt while the damage happens. For an eclipse, you'd need proper eclipse glasses.
